result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.topological_overlap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the topological overlap matrix (TOM). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11612-L11682){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.topological_overlap(return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each pair of nodes `(i, j)`, the topological overlap measures how much they share the same neighbors, normalized by the less-connected node's degree: `TOM(i, j) = (|N(i) ∩ N(j)| + a_ij) / (min(k_i, k_j) + 1 - a_ij)` where `a_ij` is 1 if `(i, j)` is an edge, `k` is degree, and `N` is the neighbor set. Diagonal entries are 1.0. This is the standard TOM from WGCNA (weighted gene co-expression network analysis), widely used in genomics for clustering genes into co-expression modules. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the TOM as a nested dictionary. Otherwise return `self` for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `{node_id: {node_id: tom_value}}` nested dictionary, or `self`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#554b98a5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="C") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") ) tom = g.topological_overlap(return_dict=True) a_id = g.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = g.get_id_from_label("B") tom[a_id][b_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: :::
